text:
Ross Colton has goals in three straight games, and one of them came on his first trip back to Denver, a goal Evan Rawal of the Denver Gazette described as the end of a disastrous Avalanche shift. Nashville has won four in a row, and Colton has been one of the reasons.

He has five goals in 17 games at about 13 minutes a night, and they're honest goals: five on 4.4 expected (the quality of his chances). Nashville has 52% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, nearly seven points better than without him, on a team that's usually outchanced.

He's a Cup winner from Tampa Bay's 2021 team who spent two seasons in Colorado. Evolving-Hockey had his team creating much more with him on the ice last season (96th percentile among forwards), while noting he played with very strong teammates there. Our projection sees about 20 goals, a better season than his nine last year. The streak will end; the role looks earned.
